top_signals.title: Ukraine's Strike in Benghazi Threatens the Deal That Keeps Libya at Peace
top_signals.summary: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian warship in Benghazi on November 22 is the spark that could ignite another civil war in Libya, just as Tripoli is pitching foreign oil companies at an energy summit for the $20 billion it says it needs to lift output to 2 million barrels a day. top_signals.title: NASA Wanted a 100-Kilowatt Reactor on the Moon but Is Settling for 20
top_signals.summary: In August 2025, Washington promised a 100-kilowatt nuclear reactor on the Moon by 2030, ahead of China and Russia. "We're in a race to the moon, in a race with China to the moon," NASA's then-interim chief Sean Duffy said, warning that whoever landed a reactor first could declare a "keep-out zone" around it. But the reactor NASA put out to bid on November 23 is one-fifth that size. top_signals.title: When the Grid Fails, Solar Does Not Wait for the State
top_signals.summary: Most power systems are built from the center outward. A government plans power stations. A utility signs fuel contracts, builds transmission lines and connects households. Large investors finance assets expected to operate for decades. The model assumes a state capable of making decisions, enforcing contracts and protecting infrastructure. In fragile and conflict-affected countries, those assumptions can disappear before electricity demand does. Syria offers a striking alternative. top_signals.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
top_signals.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers.
